item.title: Question a Reporting-Based Repair Queue
item.audience: a city committee considering road repair priorities
item.prompt_text: A city proposes ranking small road repairs by the number of reports it receives. Supporters argue that the count is visible to the public and responds to concern quickly. A neighbourhood survey suggests several residents submit weekly reports on the same unrepaired issue, while streets used by people without reliable internet may be reported less often. Write a consultation response that distinguishes visibility from need, proposes a fairer starting method, and explains how the city could tell whether the method improves decisions.
item.target_grammar: Concessive clauses; precise attribution; carefully bounded claims about measurement.
item.target_structure: Fair account of the proposal → how the count can diverge from need → a workable decision rule → a public check.

checklist.point: Explain the appeal of a public count without accepting it as a complete ranking.
Show how repeat reports and uneven access affect the available evidence.
Propose a method that keeps reports useful while introducing comparable evidence.
Explain how to check results across areas rather than just count completed jobs.
